Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 49, verse 4–5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are three reports.

The first: "The Banu Tamim came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and called out at the door: 'O Muhammad, come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace.' He came out, saying: 'That is only Allah.' They said: 'We are people of the Banu Tamim. We have come with our poet and our orator, to contend with you in poetry and to boast against you.' He said: 'I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast, but bring forth what you have.' Then al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: 'Stand up and mention your virtue and the virtue of your people.' So he stood and mentioned that. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then commanded Thabit ibn Qays, and he replied to him. Their poet stood up, and Hassan answered him. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said: 'By Allah, I do not know what this matter is! Our orator spoke, and their orator's speech was better; our poet spoke, and their poet was more eloquent.' Then he drew near and embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them gifts and clothed them. The voices rose and the clamour increased in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so this verse was revealed." This is the statement of Jabir ibn Abdullah, along with others. Ibn Ishaq said: It was revealed concerning the uncouth of the Banu Tamim, among whom were al-Aqra' ibn Habis, Uyayna ibn Hisn, al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, [Qays ibn Asim al-Minqari], Khalid ibn Malik, Suwayd ibn Hisham, and they were two men of Nahshal, al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad, Ata' ibn Habis, and WakI' ibn WakI'. (p-459)

The second: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment against the Banu al-Anbar and appointed over them Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari. When they learned of this, they fled and left their families behind, so Uyayna took them captive. Their men came seeking to ransom the captives, and they arrived at midday while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was napping. They began calling out, 'O Muhammad, come out to us,' until they woke him, and so this verse was revealed." This was stated by Ibn Abbas.

The third: Some people of the Arabs said to one another: "Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we will be the happiest of people to have him, and if he is a king, we will live under his wing." So they came and began calling out, "O Muhammad, O Muhammad," and this verse was revealed. [Zayd ibn Arqam stated this.]

As for "al-Hujurat" (the chambers): Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Aishah, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, and Ibn Ya'mar, [and Abu Ja'far, and Shayba], read it with a fatha on the jim (ـَ). Ibn Qutaybah said: The singular of al-Hujurat is hujrah, like zulmah and zulumat. The exegetes said: They called out from behind the chambers only because they did not know in which of the rooms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, patience would have been better for them. Regarding the aspect in which it would have been better for them, there are two views.

One: It would have been better for them in what they came for, namely the ransom of their families; had they been patient, he would have released their captives without ransom. This was stated by Muqatil.

The exegetes said: They called out from behind the chambers only because they did not know in which of the rooms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, patience would have been better for them. Regarding the aspect in which it would have been better for them, there are two views.

One: It would have been better for them in what they came for, namely the ransom of their families; had they been patient, he would have released their captives without ransom. This was stated by Muqatil.

The second: It would have been better for their manners in obedience to Allah and His Messenger. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is, toward those among them who repent.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 49, verses 6–8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If a deviator comes to you with a report, verify it﴾. It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqba. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him to the Banu al-Mustaliq to collect their zakat, and there had been enmity between him and them in the Jahiliyya. He travelled part of the way, then became afraid and turned back, saying: "They have withheld the zakat and wanted to kill me." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cancelled the dispatch to them, and this verse was revealed. I have mentioned the story in full in my book "al-Mughni" and in "al-Hada'iq". I have mentioned the meaning of "fa-tabayyanu" (verify) in surah al-Nisa' [4:94]. "Naba'" means report, and "an" (that) here means "lest". "Jahala" (ignorance) here means that one does not know the condition of the people. ﴿Lest you harm a people in ignorance and then become, over what you have done﴾, through striking them by mistake, ﴿regretful﴾.

Then He warned them, saying: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: if you lie to him, Allah will inform him and you will be disgraced. Then He said: ﴿Were he to obey you in much of the matter﴾, meaning: in what you report to him falsely, ﴿you would surely be in difficulty﴾, meaning: you would fall into hardship. Ibn Qutayba said: it is harm and corruption. Others said: it is sin and destruction. This is because when the Muslims heard that those people had disbelieved, they said: "Send to them, O Messenger of Allah, and make war on them and kill them." Then He addressed the believers, saying: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and disobedience﴾. Then He returned to speaking about them, saying: ﴿Those are the rightly guided﴾, meaning: those who are guided to the good of affairs, ﴿as a bounty from Allah﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: He did that for you as a bounty, that is, for favour and blessing.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 49, verses 9–10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ [49:9], the verse, concerning the cause of its revelation there are two accounts.

The first: what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, who said: "It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'If only you would go to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy.' So he mounted a donkey and the Muslims set off walking with him. When the Prophet (ﷺ) reached him, he said: 'Keep away from me! By Allah, the stench of your donkey has offended me.' A man of the Ansar said: 'By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah is better smelling than you!' Then a man of ʿAbd Allah's people became angry for him, and each of them was angered by his companions, so there was a striking among them with palm stalks, hands and sandals. It has reached us that the verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ ..." And both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to visit Saʿd ibn ʿUbada, and he passed by a gathering in which was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha. Ibn Ubayy covered his face with his garment and said: 'Do not raise dust over us.' So he mentioned the hadith, and that (p-463) the Muslims, the polytheists and the Jews abused one another." I have mentioned the hadith in full in al-Mughni and al-Hada'iq. Muqatil said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stopped by the Ansar while he was on his donkey, and the donkey urinated. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy said: 'Uff!' and held his nose. ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha said: 'By Allah, it is better smelling than you!' Between the people of Ibn Ubayy and Ibn Rawaha there was a striking with sandals, hands and palm fronds, and this verse was revealed."

The second: that it was revealed concerning two men of the Ansar who had a dispute over a right between them. One of them said: "I will certainly take my right by force," relying on the multitude of his clan; the other called him to be judged by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The matter between them continued until some of them grabbed others with hands and sandals. This was reported by Qatada. Mujahid said: the two groups are the Aws and the Khazraj; they fought with sticks among themselves. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Mas'ud and Abu 'Imran al-Jawni read "iqtatala" (fa'ala, dual masculine). Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji, Abu al-Jawn and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read "iqtatalata" with a ta' and an alif after the lam, as the dual feminine form. Al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Suddi said: ﴿So make peace between them﴾ by calling them to the judgment of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and by their acceptance of what it contains for them and against them. ﴿But if one of them transgresses﴾ — it seeks what is not its due and does not return to reconciliation — ﴿then fight the one that transgresses until it returns﴾, i.e., returns ﴿to the command of Allah﴾, i.e., to His obedience in the reconciliation which He has commanded.

(p-464) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And act justly﴾, i.e., be even-handed in reconciling between them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ [49:10]. Al-Zajjaj said: when they agree in their religion, they return by their agreement to the root of lineage, since they all descend from Adam and Eve; but when their religions differ, they separate in lineage.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So make peace between your two brothers﴾. Most readers recite "bayna akhawaykum" with a ya' as the dual. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'awiya, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Ibn Jubayr, [Qatada], Abu al-'Aliya, Ibn Ya'mar, Ibn Abi 'Abla and Ya'qub read "bayna ikhwatikum" with a ta' and a kasra on the hamza, as the plural. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, Abu Razin, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi and Ibn Sirin read "bayna ikhwanikum" with a nun and an alif before it. Qatada said: by this he means the Aws and the Khazraj.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 49, verse 11:

(p-465) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people⦆ This verse was revealed for three occasions. As for the first part, up to His saying, ﴿perhaps they are better than them﴾, it was revealed for one occasion, and concerning it there are two statements.

One of them: "Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came one day wanting to draw near to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had deafness. He said to a man in front of him: 'Make room.' The man said to him: 'You have found a seat.' So he sat down angrily. Then the man said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am so-and-so.' Thabit said: 'You are the son of so-and-so?!' and he mentioned a mother of his for whom he used to be reproached in the Jahiliyyah. The man lowered his head in shame, and there was revealed His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they are better than them﴾." This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: The delegation of Tamim mocked the poor companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of the shabbiness of their condition, so this verse was revealed. This was said by al-Dahhak and Muqatil.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿nor women [ridicule] other women﴾, it was revealed for one occasion, and concerning it there are three statements.

(p-466) One of them: The wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reproached Umm Salamah for her shortness, so this [verse] was revealed. This was said by Anas ibn Malik. Muqatil claimed that 'A'ishah mocked Umm Salamah's shortness.

The second: Two of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mocked Umm Salamah, the wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Umm Salamah had gone out one day having tied one end of her outer garment at her waist and let the other end hang behind her, and she did not know it. So one of them said to the other: "Look at what is behind Umm Salamah, it is like a dog's tongue." This was said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: "Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'The women reproach me and say: O Jewess, daughter of Jews!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Why did you not say: My father is Harun, my paternal uncle is Musa, and my husband is Muhammad?'" So this verse was revealed. 'Ikrimah related it from Ibn 'Abbas.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not defame one another, nor call each other by nicknames⦆, it was revealed for one occasion, and concerning it there are three statements.

One of them: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah and they had nicknames by which they called one another, so a man would call another man by his nickname. It was said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, they dislike this,' so there was revealed (p-467) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames⦆." This was said by Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak.

The second: Abu Dharr had a dispute with a man, and the man said to him: "O son of the Jewess!" So there was revealed: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames⦆. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari had an exchange with 'Abdullah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami. He said to him: "O bedouin!" and 'Abdullah said to him: "O Jew!" So there was revealed concerning the two of them: ﴿And do not defame yourselves, nor call each other by nicknames⦆. This was said by Muqatil.

As for the exegesis: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿let not a people ridicule another people⦆ means: let not a rich man mock a poor man, nor one whose sin is concealed mock one whose sin is not concealed, nor one of noble lineage mock one of base lineage, and similar things by which one belittles another, perhaps they are better than him in the sight of Allah. We have explained in [al-Baqarah: 54] that "qawm" (people) is the name for men to the exclusion of women, and for this reason He said: ﴿nor women [ridicule] other women⦆. "Talmizu" means to find fault, and its explanation has already preceded [at-Tawbah: 58]. What is meant by "anfus" (selves) here is brothers. The meaning: do not find fault with your brethren among the Muslims, for they are like yourselves. "Tanabuz" is a reciprocal form from "nabz," which is a verbal noun, and "nabaz" is the noun. "Alqab" is the plural of "laqab" (nickname), which is a name by which a person is called other than the name he was given. Ibn Qutaybah said: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames⦆ means: do not summon one another by them. "Alqab" and "anbaz" are one and the same, and from it comes the hadith: "Nabzuhum al-Rafidah," meaning: their nickname is "the Rafidah." There are four statements of the exegetes concerning what is meant by these nicknames.

One of them: reproaching the penitent for evil deeds he had committed. Narrated by 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: calling him, after his Islam, by his religion before Islam, as saying to a Jew who has become Muslim: "O Jew!" This is also related from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Qurazi said likewise.

The third: a man saying to another: "O unbeliever! O hypocrite!" This was said by 'Ikrimah.

The fourth: calling him by evil deeds, as saying: "O fornicator! O thief! O sinner!" This was said by Ibn Zayd. The people of knowledge said: What is meant by these nicknames is what the one addressed by them dislikes, or what is counted as a blame against him. As for the nicknames that bring praise and are truthful, they are not disliked, as was said to Abu Bakr: "'Atiq," to 'Umar: "Al-Faruq," to 'Uthman: "Dhu al-Nurayn," to 'Ali: "Abu Turab" (p-469) and to Khalid: "Sayf Allah," and the like. His saying: ﴿How evil is the name of wickedness (fusuq)⦆ means: calling him a sinner or an unbeliever when he has believed. ﴿And whoever does not repent⦆ from the mutual calling by nicknames, ﴿those are the wrongdoers (zalimun)⦆. Concerning this there are two statements.

One of them: those who harm themselves through their disobedience. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: they are more unjust than those who said those things to them. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 49, verse 12:**

(p-٤٧٠) Allah's words: ﴿Avoid much suspicion﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah the Exalted forbade the believer to think ill of a fellow believer. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is a man who hears a statement from his brother that he did not intend as evil, or who enters a place without intending anything bad by it, and his Muslim brother sees him and thinks ill of him. Al-Zajjaj said: It is to think ill of people of goodness. As for people of evil and sin, we may think of them what has become apparent from them.

Qadi Abu Ya'la said: This verse indicates that not all suspicion has been forbidden, and suspicion is of four kinds: forbidden, commanded, permitted, and recommended. The forbidden kind is ill opinion of Allah the Exalted, while the obligatory kind is good opinion of Allah. Likewise, ill opinion of the Muslims whose outward state is uprightness ('adala) is forbidden. As for the commanded kind of suspicion, it is that which is not founded on evidence that leads to knowledge of it, and we have been commanded to implement a ruling on it, to rely on the stronger assumption (ghalib al-zann), and to apply the ruling based on it, which is obligatory. This is like what we have been commanded to observe: accepting the testimony of upright witnesses, determining the qibla by inquiry (taharri), assessing the value of consumed goods, and the compensation for injuries (arsh al-jinayat) whose amounts have not been fixed by revelation. For these and similar matters we have been commanded to follow the rulings of stronger assumptions. As for the permitted kind of suspicion, it is like the doubtful person in prayer when he is the imam: the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to seek the correct course and act upon what is most likely in his assumption. If he does so, it is permitted; and if he turns away from it to build upon certainty, that is also allowed. Abu Hurayra narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you suspect, do not verify." This is the suspicion that arises in a person's heart about his brother concerning something that calls for doubt, so he should not pursue it to confirm it. As for the recommended kind of suspicion, it is good opinion of a Muslim brother, which is recommended and rewarded. As for what has been related in the hadith: "Guard yourselves against people through ill opinion," the meaning is guarding wealth, such as one saying: If I leave my door open, I fear thieves.

(p-٤٧١) Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾. The exegetes said: It is the suspicion of evil about one's Muslim brother that a person speaks out. If he does not speak of it, there is no harm. Some scholars held that he is sinful for the suspicion itself even if he does not voice it.

Allah's words: ﴿And do not spy﴾. Abu Razin, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Ibn Sirin, Abu Raja', and Ibn Ya'mar read it with the letter ḥā' (التَّحَسُّسُ). Abu 'Ubayda said: tajassus (التَّجَسُّسُ) and taḥassus (التَّحَسُّسُ) are the same, meaning searching out, and from it comes the word jasus (spy). It is narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir that he said: tajassus with the letter jīm means searching for people's faults, and with ḥā' it means eavesdropping on people's conversations. The exegetes said: tajassus is searching for the faults and shortcomings of Muslims. The meaning is: let none of you search for the defect of his brother in order to uncover it, since Allah has concealed it. It was said to Ibn Mas'ud: "This is al-Walid ibn 'Uqba, whose beard drips with wine." He said: We have been forbidden to spy, but if something becomes apparent to us, we will take him to account for it.

Allah's words: ﴿And do not backbite one another﴾. That is, let none of you slander another in his absence with what would hurt him. Abu Hurayra narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "What is backbiting (ghiba)?" He said: "Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "What if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is true of your brother, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him."

(p-٤٧٢) Then Allah set forth an example for backbiting, saying: ﴿Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ Nafi' read mayyitan (مَيْتًا) with a shadda (مَيِّتًا). Al-Zajjaj said: The explanation is that mentioning someone with evil in his absence is like eating his flesh while he is dead and does not feel it. Qadi Abu Ya'la said: This is an emphasis on the prohibition of backbiting, because eating the flesh of a Muslim is forbidden, and because human nature naturally recoils from it, so backbiting should be in the same position of aversion.

Allah's words: ﴿so you would detest it﴾. Al-Dahhak and 'Asim al-Jahdari read it as fa-kuvvihtumūhu (فَكُرِّهْتُمُوهُ), with a raised kāf and a shadda on the rā'. Al-Farra' said: That is, "and you have indeed detested it, so do not do it." And whoever reads fa-karihtumūhu (فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ) means: it has been made hateful to you. The meaning is one. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: just as you dislike eating the flesh of your dead brother, so likewise avoid mentioning him with evil in his absence.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 49, verse 13:

(p. 473) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾. There are three opinions regarding its occasion of revelation.

The first: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and his saying to the man who did not make room for him: "You are the son of so-and-so." We have already mentioned this from Ibn Abbas in his commentary on His saying: ﴿Let not a people ridicule [another] people﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11].

The second: "When the day of the Conquest came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Bilal, and he climbed onto the roof of the Ka'bah and called the adhan, intending by that to humiliate the polytheists. When he gave the adhan, Attab ibn Usayd said: 'Praise be to Allah who took Usayd before this day.' al-Harith ibn Hisham said: 'Has Muhammad not found anyone other than this black crow to be a muezzin?!' Suhayl ibn Amr said: 'If Allah dislikes something, He will change it.' Abu Sufyan said: 'As for me, I will not say anything, for if I said something, the heavens would surely bear witness against me and the earth would surely inform of me.' Then this verse was revealed." Related by Muqatil.

The third: "A black slave fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited him. Then he died, and [the Messenger of Allah ﷺ] took charge of washing him, shrouding him and burying him. This affected the Companions, and so this verse was revealed." Related by Yazid ibn Shajara.

As for what is meant by "male and female," it is Adam and Hawwa' (Eve). The meaning is: you are equal in lineage, and this is a rebuke against boasting about ancestry.

As for ash-shu'ub (nations, peoples), it is the plural of sha'b, which is a great tribe (al-hayy al-'azim), like Mudar and Rabi'ah; and the qaba'il (tribes) are below it, like Bakr from Rabi'ah and Tamim from (p. 474) Mudar. This is the view of the majority of the exegetes (mufassirin) and the lexicographers (ahl al-lughah). 'Ata' narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "By ash-shu'ub he means the mawali (non-Arab clients), and by al-qaba'il he means the Arabs." Abu Razin said: "Ash-shu'ub are the people of the mountains who do not claim allegiance to anyone, and al-qaba'il are the tribes of the Arabs." Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: "It has been said that al-qaba'il are the roots, and ash-shu'ub are the branches that spread out from them, and this is the opposite of the first view."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿that you may know one another﴾. That is, so that some of you may know others regarding closeness and distance of lineage. Az-Zajjaj said: "The meaning is: We made you thus, that you may know one another, not that you may boast." Then He informed them that the most honoured of them in His sight is the most righteous of them.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Ibn Ya'mar, and Aban from 'Asim read: "li-ta'rifu" (لِتَعْرِفُوا), with a sukun on the ʿayn and a kasrah on the rā', without an alif. Mujahid, Abu al-Mutawakkil, and Ibn Muhaysin read: "li-ta'arafu" (لِتَّعارَفُوا), with a single shaddah-ed tā' and an alif, the rā' with a fatha and not shaddah-ed. Abu Nuhayk and al-A'mash read: "li-tatA'arafu" (لِتَتَعَرَّفُوا), with two tā's, the rā' with a fatha and shaddah-ed, without an alif.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed the most honoured of you﴾. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Mujahid, and Abu al-Jawza' read: "anna" (أنَّ), with a fatha on the hamzah. Al-Farra' said: "Whoever reads 'an' with a fatha, it is as if he said: 'that you may know that the noble one is the righteous one.' If it were so, it would be 'li-ta'rifu,' but it is permissible to say 'li-ta'arafu' in the sense of: 'that some of you may make others know that the most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.'"

(p-٤٧٥) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The bedouins say, "We have believed."﴾ Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning the bedouins of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma. Others described their condition, saying: They came to Madinah in a year of drought. They displayed Islam while they were not believers. They corrupted the roads of Madinah with their filth, and they inflated their prices. They used to remind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of their favours, saying: "We came to you with our burdens and our dependants, and we did not fight you." So this verse was revealed concerning them. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the bedouins of Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam, Ashja' and Ghifar, [and they are the ones Allah mentioned in Surah [al-Fath]. They used to say, "We have believed in Allah," so that they would be safe for themselves]. When they were called to go forth to al-Hudaybiyya, they stayed behind, so this verse was revealed concerning them. Muqatil said: Their dwellings were between Makkah and Madinah. Whenever a detachment (sariyya, a small military expedition) from the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by them, they would say, "We have believed," so that they would be safe for their lives and their property. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for al-Hudaybiyya, he called them to go forth with him, but they did not go forth with him.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: You have not believed.﴾ That is: you have not affirmed (the truth). ﴿But say, "We have submitted."﴾ Ibn Qutayba said: That is, we have surrendered out of fear of the sword, and we have yielded. Al-Zajjaj said: Islam (al-Islam, submission) is the display of humility and acceptance of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought, and by it blood is protected. If there is accompanying belief and affirmation in the heart, then that is faith (iman). Allah therefore excluded these people from faith by His saying: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts.﴾ That is: you have not affirmed; you only embraced Islam to seek protection from killing. Muqatil said: "Wa lamma" carries the meaning of "wa lam": ﴿and affirmation has not entered your hearts.﴾

(p-٤٧٧) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. Ibn Abbas said: That is, if you make your faith sincere. ﴿He will not deprive you (la yalitkum) of your deeds.﴾ Abu Amr read "ya'litkum" with an alif and a hamza. It is also narrated from him with a silent alif and without the hamza. The rest read "yalitkum" without an alif and without a hamza. So the reading of Abu Amr is from alata yaʾlitu, and the reading of the others is from lata yalitu. Al-Farra' said: They are two dialects. Al-Zajjaj said: Their meaning is one. The meaning is: He will not diminish you. Abu Ubayda said: In it there are three dialects: alata yaʾlitu, whose pattern is afaka yafiku; alata yulitu (sic, as in the source's form), whose pattern is aqala yuqilu; and lata yalitu. Ru'ba said:

"And many a night, laden with dew, I traveled, and the lion did not turn me from its journeys."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿of your deeds﴾. That is: of their reward. Then He described the truthful in their faith by the verse that follows this one. The meaning of ﴿they doubt not﴾ (yartabu) is: they do not doubt. Jihad was mentioned because jihad alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was obligatory at that time. ﴿Those are the truthful.﴾ [in their faith.] When these two verses were revealed, they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) swearing that they were believers and truthful, so [this verse] was revealed.

The meaning is: Will you inform [Allah] of the religion you hold? (p-٤٧٨) That is: He knows that, and does not need your informing Him. Concerning them was revealed His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They count it as a favour to you that they have embraced Islam.﴾ They said: "We have embraced Islam and did not fight you." [And Allah knows best.]
